subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: I can ask: What's your favourite book?
I can describe a book with very: very interesting, very scary.
I can write about my favourite book.

tf.s: We ask "What's your favourite book?" to know the book someone likes best.
tf.why: Favourite means the one you like best.

tf.s: A good answer is "My favourite book is Cinderella."
tf.why: We start with "My favourite book is ...".

tf.s: "Is it very scary?" can get the answer "Yes, it is."
The short answer "No, it is." is correct.

tf.why: Very big is more than big.

tf.s: "Snow White" is the name of a colour in this lesson.
tf.why: Snow White is the name of a story book.

tf.s: "It's very scary" means the book is very happy.
tf.why: Scary means it makes you feel afraid.

hunt.q: A very loud thing is very ___

mcq.q: Which question asks about a favourite book?
mcq.why: "Favourite" means the one you like best.

mcq.q: Which word goes before an adjective to make it stronger?
mcq.why: Very makes it stronger: very big.

mcq.q: Which of these is a story book in the lesson?
mcq.why: Jack and the Beanstalk is in the lesson.

mcq.q: Complete: My favourite book is Jack and the Beanstalk. It's very ___.
mcq.why: In the lesson, Jack and the Beanstalk is very scary.

mcq.q: Your friend asks: Is it very interesting? Your book is interesting. You say:
Put the words in order: book / My / is / favourite / Snow White
o: My favourite book is Snow White.
My book favourite is Snow White.
Favourite my book is Snow White.
Snow White book is my favourite is.
mcq.why: My favourite book is Snow White.

mcq.q: Which is the right order for the dialogue?
o: What's your favourite book? – Jack and the Beanstalk. – It's very scary.
It's very scary. – What's your favourite book? – Jack and the Beanstalk.
Jack and the Beanstalk. – It's very scary. – What's your favourite book?
It's very scary. – Jack and the Beanstalk. – What's your favourite book?
mcq.why: First the question, then the book, then the adjective.
Very goes before an adjective, not before "a book".
